 Coby White, Brandon Miller, Grant Williams, Naz Reid and Moussa Diabaté will start Tuesday’s game against the Lakers. 
 Hornets head coach Charles Lee has changed his starting lineup, with Williams replacing Sion James. Williams played 20 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Clippers, hitting three three-pointers and scoring 11 points. While a solid defender, James is limited as a scorer, which may have factored into the lineup change. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Brandon Miller (hip) is not on the injury report for Sunday’s game against the Clippers. 
 Miller will be back following a two-game absence with a hip strain. Sion James has been starting in his place, so he will likely return to the bench with Miller back in the mix. 
 Grant Williams 
 CHA 
 Forward 
 #2 
 Grant Williams made his season debut on Thursday and contributed 11 points (3-of-5 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, one block and two three-pointers against the Suns. 
 Suiting up for the first time this season after missing the start of the year with a hamstring strain, Williams was able to make an impact immediately. Despite playing just 16 minutes, Williams was able to space the floor and score in double figures. They also outscored the Suns by 11 points when he was on the floor, which was the best mark on the team by far. Williams isn’t a standard-league option, but he is a solid depth piece for Charlotte. 
 Grant Williams 
 CHA 
 Forward 
 #2 
 Grant Williams (hamstring) will make his season debut Thursday against the Suns. 
 Given Charlotte’s multiple injuries, Williams may not have the luxury of being eased back into action. He’s not a guy to get into fantasy lineups right away, but managers in deeper leagues should keep an eye on his workload. 
 Grant Williams 
 CHA 
 Forward 
 #2 
 Grant Williams (hamstring) is probable for Thursday’s game against the Suns. 
 Williams could make his first appearance of the season on Thursday. While he doesn’t play the same position as Kon Knueppel (hamstring) or Brandon Miller (hip), Williams’ return would give the Hornets much-needed depth in the frontcourt. 
 Brandon Miller 
 CHA 
 Forward 
 #24 
 Brandon Miller (hip) is out for Thursday’s game against the Suns. 
 Miller will miss a second straight game as he recovers from a strained right hip. Sion James started Monday’s win over the Cavaliers and should continue to do so until Miller returns. 
 Sion James 
 CHA 
 Guard 
 #4 
 Coby White, Sion James, Grayson Allen, Naz Reid and Ryan Kalkbrenner will start Monday’s game against the Cavaliers. 
 The Hornets will not have Brandon Miller for Monday’s game, opening up a spot in the starting lineup. The void will be filled by James, whose presence should allow White to spend more time playing off the ball. 
 Kon Knueppel 
 CHA 
 Guard-Forward 
 #7 
 Kon Knueppel (hamstring) will be re-evaluated in four weeks. 
 Knueppel strained his left hamstring before training camp and did not make his season debut until Wednesday. Unfortunately, he left after six minutes and has been diagnosed with another strain of the same hamstring. Knueppel’s absence should push Sion James back into the starting lineup, but he offers limited fantasy value as a streamer. 
 Dennis Schröder 
 CHA 
 Guard 
 #17 
 Dennis Schröder (thigh) is questionable to play against the Celtics on Friday. 
 Schröder could miss a game for the first time this season. Coby White is healthy, but he’s on a strict minutes restriction. Rookie Christian Anderson has been assigned to the G League, so Sion James, who is already starting, would likely operate as the backup point guard if Schröder is out. 
 Kon Knueppel 
 CHA 
 Guard-Forward 
 #7 
 Kon Knueppel (leg) will not return to Wednesday’s game against the Nets. 
 Making his first appearance of the season after straining his left hamstring before training camp, Knueppel played six minutes before returning to the locker room during the first quarter. The Hornets have said the injury is left leg soreness, which is concerning, even though they didn’t mention the hamstring specifically. Sion James would be the likely replacement in the starting lineup if Knueppel misses time. 
 Kon Knueppel 
 CHA 
 Guard-Forward 
 #7 
 Kon Knueppel (hamstring) has been upgraded to available to play against the Nets on Wednesday. 
 Knueppel missed the first eight games of the season, but he’ll be able to suit up against Brooklyn. It’s worth noting that Coby White (calf) made his season debut in Charlotte’s last game and played 16 minutes as a starter. The lopsided score could have been a factor, but the expectation should be that Knueppel replaces Sion James as a starter, though he likely plays a small role in this game. Grayson Allen will likely lose out on minutes with Knueppel back.

 Damian Lillard finished Tuesday’s loss to the Timberwolves with 25 points (8-of-19 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, one steal and five three-pointers.
 Lillard finished with 25 points, but his layup attempt in the final seconds, which would have given Portland the win, was blocked by Minnesota’s Trey Lyles. He’s scored at least 20 points in seven of the 10 games Portland has played since losing Ja Morant to a hamstring injury, providing top-100 fantasy value. Portland visits Milwaukee on Thursday in Lillard’s first game against the Bucks since being waived in the summer of 2025.

 LaMelo Ball recorded 18 points (7-of-17 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), nine rebounds, two assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Trail Blazers.
 After recording at least five assists in five straight games, Ball had two in the Timberwolves’ two games against Portland. The good news for the Timberwolves was that they won both games, but that low assist number was a surprise. Ball finished Tuesday’s win one rebound shy of a double-double, offering unexpected value in that category. Even with the recent low assist numbers, field-goal percentage and turnovers remain Ball’s biggest issues in category leagues. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Jaden McDaniels amassed 22 points (10-of-16 FGs), five rebounds, four assists, three steals, one block and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Trail Blazers.
 While McDaniels’ offensive production has been consistent throughout the season, fantasy managers may have hoped for a bit more from him in the aftermath of Anthony Edwards’ knee injury. He’s scored 20+ points three times since Edwards was injured in an October 26 loss to the Cavaliers, and his 23 points against the Trail Blazers matched his season high. That said, even with the scoring, McDaniels is still providing top-50 value in category leagues.

 Ayo Dosunmu accounted for 30 points (11-of-19 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, one steal and seven three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Trail Blazers.
 After scoring eight points on 3-of-11 shooting in Monday’s win over the Trail Blazers, Dosunmu rebounded in a big way in Tuesday’s rematch. Making his 10th straight start for the injured Anthony Edwards, Ayo recorded his first 30-point stat line of the season while shooting a high percentage from the field. Add in the rebounds, assists and three-pointers, and this was an excellent night for those rostering Dosunmu.

 Stephon Castle recorded 10 points (3-of-11 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), two rebounds, seven assists and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Pistons.
 Castle didn’t have a good night shooting the basketball, but he did provide solid value in the assists column. He has recorded six or more assists in three of his last four games and is averaging 5.5 assists per game for the season. De’Aaron Fox (6/2/2/2) also struggled against the Pistons, shooting 3-of-10 from the field, offering even less value to fantasy managers than Castle.

 Devin Vassell finished Tuesday’s loss to the Pistons with 12 points (4-of-10 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, four assists, one steal and two three-pointers.
 A 2-of-4 night from beyond the arc isn’t much, but it was a step in the right direction for Vassell, who was 0-of-6 in wins over the Warriors and Jazz. A career 37.0 percent shooter from three, Devin entered Tuesday making a career-low 31.4 percent of his attempts. Fantasy managers rostering Vassell received solid value in rebounds and assists on Tuesday, but consistent three-point shooting is key for him.
